overview.summary: This codebase is a React and TypeScript application built with Vite, focused on a storybook-driven interface for guiding users through setup and workflow steps. The structure is minimal, centered around the 'src' module containing all UI components and pages, with a small root-level configuration layer.

modules.name: src
modules.responsibility: Contains all UI components, pages, and business logic for the storybook-guided user flow.

modules.name: __root__
modules.responsibility: Holds configuration and build-level files such as vite.config.ts, package.json, and other root metadata.

connections.note: Root configuration files (vite.config.ts, tsconfig.json) enable the build system to compile and serve the src module.

flows.name: User Authentication Flow
flows.description: Handles user login, signup, logout, and session restoration using token management and repository key tracking.
risks: Token might be stored insecurely if not handled via secure HTTP-only cookies or localStorage with proper sanitization.
Session restoration could bypass authentication if token is expired or tampered with without validation.
Repository key tracking might leak sensitive data if not bound to authenticated user context.

Global error handler; ensures stale or revoked tokens automatically terminate sessions.

flows.name: Repository Management
flows.description: Manages repository selection, switching, and addition, updating the active workspace context.
risks: Failure to properly reset workspace state when switching repositories may lead to stale data display.
Direct mutation of global state via connectedRepoKey without proper synchronization could cause race conditions.
Missing validation on repository addition may allow invalid or duplicate entries in the UI.

flows.name: Workspace Navigation
flows.description: Enables creation, renaming, deletion, and restructuring of workspaces and their nested nodes through interactive UI actions and state updates.
risks: Improper state synchronization between UI and backend may cause inconsistent node hierarchies.
Drag-and-drop operations could misplace nodes if onNodeDrop validation is incomplete.
Renaming or deleting workspaces without confirming active references may orphan child nodes.

flows.name: Document Editing Flow
flows.description: End-to-end narrative of rich text document editing with blocks, slash commands, typing, and dynamic content updates.
risks: Missing state synchronicity between client and server during content updates
Slash command handlers not properly validated, risking injection or unintended block transformations
Block reordering without atomic commit may leave document in inconsistent state
No error handling in autoGrow or commit for malformed input or edge cases

detail.summary: End-to-end narrative of rich text document editing with blocks, slash commands, typing, and dynamic content updates.
This triggers handleSelectDoc, which updates the connectedRepoKey to ensure context matches the selected document.
DocsEditor invokes autoGrow and renders blocks based on the document’s current structure stored in state.
handleInput is called, which invokes autoGrow to adjust block height and setText to update block contents.
handleInput detects '/' and calls openSlash to show the SlashMenu component, enabling command selection.
applySlashCommand is called, which sets the block type via setType and clears the menu via closeSlash.
setType updates the block's metadata, and commit is invoked to persist the change locally before syncing.
commit calls onChange, which notifies the parent context of the document state change, triggering a re-render and eventual sync.
updateDocContent is called, which updates the document's internal representation but does not yet write to storage.
force is invoked to rebuild the document tree via buildTree, ensuring block relationships and ordering are consistent.
request is triggered with the new document content; getToken ensures authentication token is attached before sending.
force triggers a re-render of AppContent, refreshing the entire document UI to match the now-persistent state.
moveBlock is called, which updates the block order in state, applies setType if needed, and commits the change.
updateWorkspaceNodes is called if the document was moved within a workspace, ensuring sidebar reflects structural changes.
A slash command like '/date' invokes a datetime formatter that injects formatted text; this is external logic (not from state).
closeSlash is invoked via a blur or click handler, resetting UI state without committing changes.
onHide may trigger a final commit or sync call to ensure no edits are lost during navigation.

steps.name: User selects document
steps.description: User clicks on a document in the sidebar, triggering selection and loading its content into the editor.
steps.insight: This triggers handleSelectDoc, which updates the connectedRepoKey to ensure context matches the selected document.

steps.name: Render document editor
steps.description: The selected document’s content is rendered using the DocsEditor component with BlockRow and BlockGutter UI.
steps.insight: DocsEditor invokes autoGrow and renders blocks based on the document’s current structure stored in state.

steps.name: User types text
steps.description: User inputs text into an active block; input event triggers real-time update and auto-resizing.
steps.insight: handleInput is called, which invokes autoGrow to adjust block height and setText to update block contents.

steps.name: User triggers slash command
steps.description: User types '/' in a block to open the slash command menu.
steps.insight: handleInput detects '/' and calls openSlash to show the SlashMenu component, enabling command selection.

steps.name: Select slash command
steps.description: User selects a command (e.g., '/heading') from the menu; command is applied to current block.
steps.insight: applySlashCommand is called, which sets the block type via setType and clears the menu via closeSlash.

steps.name: Apply block type change
steps.description: The block’s type is updated (e.g., from 'paragraph' to 'heading') and UI re-renders accordingly.
steps.insight: setType updates the block's metadata, and commit is invoked to persist the change locally before syncing.

steps.name: Commit block state
steps.description: The updated block state is committed and marked for synchronization with the backend.
steps.insight: commit calls onChange, which notifies the parent context of the document state change, triggering a re-render and eventual sync.

steps.name: Update document content in state
steps.description: Parent App component receives the updated content and updates the document’s state in memory.
steps.insight: updateDocContent is called, which updates the document's internal representation but does not yet write to storage.

steps.name: Force recompute document tree
steps.description: Content changes require reconstruction of the document’s hierarchical block tree for rendering.
steps.insight: force is invoked to rebuild the document tree via buildTree, ensuring block relationships and ordering are consistent.

steps.name: Sync changes to backend
steps.description: The updated document is sent to the server via API request to persist changes.
steps.insight: request is triggered with the new document content; getToken ensures authentication token is attached before sending.

steps.name: Server confirms write
steps.description: Backend validates and persists document changes in the repo database.
steps.insight: The repo's document storage layer receives the payload, writes to the underlying document store, and returns success code.

steps.name: Trigger re-render of UI
steps.description: Upon successful sync, UI re-renders to reflect final state and reset transient states like typing indicators.
steps.insight: force triggers a re-render of AppContent, refreshing the entire document UI to match the now-persistent state.

steps.name: Handle block movement
steps.description: User drags a block to reorder it; this triggers a move operation with visual feedback.
steps.insight: moveBlock is called, which updates the block order in state, applies setType if needed, and commits the change.

steps.name: Update workspace structure
steps.description: If document metadata changes (e.g., title or position), the workspace hierarchy is updated.
steps.insight: updateWorkspaceNodes is called if the document was moved within a workspace, ensuring sidebar reflects structural changes.

steps.name: Dynamic content update (e.g., template insertion)
steps.description: Inserting a dynamic block (e.g., 'Today’s date') auto-populates content from external logic.
steps.insight: A slash command like '/date' invokes a datetime formatter that injects formatted text; this is external logic (not from state).

steps.name: Close slash menu on blur
steps.description: User clicks outside the menu, and it closes without applying a command.
steps.insight: closeSlash is invoked via a blur or click handler, resetting UI state without committing changes.

steps.name: Validate on exit
steps.description: When user navigates away, final state is committed and changes are queued for sync if not already sent.
steps.insight: onHide may trigger a final commit or sync call to ensure no edits are lost during navigation.

flows.name: Node Manipulation
flows.description: Allows moving, renaming, deleting, and creating nodes with drag-and-drop and keyboard support.
risks: Drag-and-drop operations may trigger inconsistent state updates if onNodeDrop is not properly synchronized with updateWorkspaceNodes.
Renaming or deleting nodes without proper confirmation could lead to irreversible data loss.
Keyboard shortcuts for node manipulation may conflict with global keydown handlers in DocsEditor or other components.
Incomplete cleanup of node references during deletion may cause memory leaks or stale UI state.

detail.summary: Allows moving, renaming, deleting, and creating nodes with drag-and-drop and keyboard support.
This function prepares the drag payload and sets up drag effects but does not modify state — it's a preparation step for user-initiated manipulation.
It evaluates node hierarchy context to allow or disallow drops, ensuring structural integrity during manipulation.

Directly mutates the internal tree structure; triggers updateWorkspaceNodes to synchronize UI state.

Called after user initiates creation via UI — typically follows NewItemInput submission or context menu selection.
Can interfere with DocsEditor's key handlers — must scope checks to focused element to avoid unintended behavior.
Bridges UI form submission with state mutation — acts as the entry point for 'Create' actions initiated by user.
Observes state changes and updates the visible tree — indirectly confirms that manipulation is successfully reflected.
Used as fallback when incremental updates (e.g., from handleRenameDocTitle) are insufficient — expensive but safe.
Not typically called during routine manipulation — only during startup or recovery — heavy operation, avoid during user interactions.
Ensures manipulation actions operate on the right data — if misconfigured, actions affect wrong workspace.
Connects document metadata to node identity — renaming may cause display inconsistencies if force is omitted.
Critical for multi-repo support — node manipulations are scoped to this key; errors here lead to cross-repo pollution.
Not directly called in manipulation flow, but required for any state-modifying API interaction — session expiry blocks writes.

Sets active context — manipulation actions (e.g., Del) affect the currently selected document node.
